children: The European Union's top official said Brussels has plans to stop children under 13 from accessing social networks and restrict what teenagers can do online.

Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission's president, on Wednesday revealed details of a plan for a new EU-wide law curbing minors' access to social networks as more countries in the bloc have started work on their own rulebooks.

Under the plans, children under 13 wouldn't have access to social media, while those between 13 and 15 would get limited access under parental supervision, and that online platforms would be obliged to ensure they are safe for young people older than that, according to von der Leyen.
She told lawmakers in Strasbourg the EU would take a gradual approach with tailored protection levels.
The commission plans to propose a so-called Kids Act this week, which would govern young people's access to platforms.

title: EU Chief Reveals Plans for Curbing Children's Access to Social Media
